Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the Irish side's response with the bat for the second time in this contest, with New Zealand enforcing follow-on. Once again for the home side, Andy Balbirnie walks out with Stephen Doheny at the top. Nathan Smith will start proceedings with the ball. Ireland trail by 311 runs.
... THIRD INNINGS ...

The final wrap and a follow on - However, it was that man Nathan Smith who stepped up yet again for New Zealand to break the defiant stand, getting the crucial breakthrough by removing Adair for a well-made 40. He picked up 6 wickets in his 14 overs, and this was his career best bowling figures in an innings. Thomas Mayes fell shortly after, leaving McBrine to play a heroic lone hand of 73 unbeaten before the tail finally ran out of answers. Ireland's first innings folded for 179 runs, and with a massive deficit of 311 runs remaining, the visitors have wasted no time in enforcing the follow-on.

The middle order fightback - Just when an early collapse looked certain, Andy McBrine and Mark Adair combined to lead a much-needed rescue mission. The duo showed immense resolve under intense pressure, steadying the rocking ship with a brilliant 116-run partnership for the seventh wicket. They dug deep, frustrated the Kiwi bowling attack, and safely guided the team out of immediate danger, offering the home fans at Belfast a glimmer of hope.

Early carnage by Nathan Smith - Ireland's response to New Zealand's massive first-innings total got off to a disastrous start as Kiwi pacer Nathan Smith ran riot. Smith turned the match on its head immediately, striking twice in his very first over for a phenomenal double-wicket maiden. The relentless seam bowler didn't stop there, tearing through the top and middle order to claim his maiden five-wicket haul. He picked up the first five wickets single-handedly. When Zak Foulkes dismissed Harry Tector shortly after, the hosts were left completely shell-shocked and teetering at a miserable 38 for 6.

New Zealand take full control - With the Ireland innings getting wrapped up at 179 in 45 overs and still 311 runs behind New Zealand's first innings total, the word coming in is that New Zealand have enforced the follow-on.

OUT! CAUGHT! The Kiwis have got their last wicket. A sharp bouncer from Ben Sears around off. Reuben Wilson sways his head to make a leave at it, but the ball thumps the gloves of the batter. The ball then lobs toward the front of Kane Williamson in the first slip region, where he dives and takes a good catch. Ireland are all out, posting 179 runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the evening session! The umpires are marching toward the center of the park. The players of New Zealand have taken their fielding positions. Andy McBrine and Mark Adair will be looking to find a good start after the Tea break. Nathan Smith will start with the proceedings with two slips and a gully. Let's play...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Ireland fights back - The two lower-order fighters are refusing to simply roll over. Adair has shown his calm to successfully defend his wicket, while McBrine has combined grit with some elegant strokeplay to frustrate a New Zealand attack that will feel the innings should already be over. McBrine is looking sturdy with his back foot strokes, and as the game progressed, he had more clarity in his shot selection. McBrine got his sixth Test half-century moments before the Tea break was taken, and right now he and Adair have a partnership of 101 runs. After the Tea break, it would be interesting to see how the Kiwi bowlers shape up to conclude on Day 2 in this final session. Join us at 3.30 pm GMT to witness the action in the last session of Day 2!

Adair and McBrine to rescue - Ireland trailed by 456 runs coming into this session, and despite the best efforts of a few individuals to hang around, the New Zealand bowlers kept the pressure suffocating and the scoreboard moving painfully slowly for the hosts.  The one genuine bright spot of the afternoon has been the partnership between Mark Adair and Andy McBrine down the batting order. Ireland were 38 for 6 in 10 overs, but it has been the seventh wicket partnership that is giving the Irish supporters hope.

TEA ON DAY 2 - What a session it was for both sides! The Kiwi bowlers started magnificently, picking two of the wickets before the Lunch break, and it's not a surprise that they kept that pressure on the hosts even after the Lunch break. Ireland resumed the afternoon session, facing the monumental task of batting against a New Zealand attack brimming with pace and confidence. The top order had already crumbled under pressure during the morning, and the second session offered little early respite. Wickets continued to fall as New Zealand's seamers, led by the rapid duo Nathan Smith and Zakary Foulkes, relentlessly exploited the surface, exposing Ireland's fragile batting lineup by nipping the deliveries back and forth, utilizing the overcasted condition exceptionally well.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! It has been a phase of play that has been dominated by the visitors. After posting a mammoth total and declaring right before the break, the visitors have breezed past the batting unit of Ireland in the post-Lunch session as well. The top and middle order of the home side has been sent back packing, and it is now the duo of their pace spearhead Mark Adair and spin maestro Andy McBrine to show some fight. Ireland needs a massive rescue act just to stay in the game, while NZ will be eager to wrap up the innings quickly.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second session of Day 2. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Harry Tector and Andy Balbirnie will resume their innings. They desperately need a long partnership. Nathan Smith will start with the ball. Let's go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

The hosts have a mountain to climb - Skipper Andrew Balbirnie and Harry Tector are currently on strike, showing some grit to guide Ireland to the lunch break at a shaky 20/2. The hosts desperately need a massive, heroic stand from these two to rebuild the innings and somehow get Ireland back into this game. They trail by a mammoth 470 runs. Can they produce something special against a red hot bowling attack? We will find out soon. Join us right after the lunch break at 1.10 pm GMT for all the live action.

Nathan Smith's double-wicket nightmare - Ireland’s response started in the worst possible fashion under relentless pressure from the Kiwi bowlers. Nathan Smith turned the game on its head immediately, bowling a phenomenal first over that ended as a double-wicket maiden. He extracted lethal movement to dismiss Stephen Doheny and Cade Carmichael for ducks, leaving the Irish top order completely shell-shocked within the first six balls of the innings.

The Kiwi declaration - New Zealand started their day from an overnight score of 333/5, with Tom Blundell and Dean Foxcroft continuing to punish the Irish bowling attack. The duo stitched together a superb 158-run partnership before Blundell suffered an unfortunate dismissal, walking back after a magnificent 186. The Blackcaps delayed their declaration to let the debutant Foxcroft reach his maiden Test ton, but heartbreak struck when he fell on a nervous 98. New Zealand finally declared their innings at a colossal 490/8.
